title: Non-Hermitian control of helicity-selective antiferromagnetic resonance
authors: Masato Todani, Satoshi Iihama, Yuto Moritake, Takeo Kato
abstract: We study non-Hermitian antiferromagnetic resonance in an antiferromagnetic insulator/nonmagnetic metal junction with sublattice-dependent damping and spin-orbit torque. By formulating the linearized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation as a 2x2 non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem, we derive the complex resonance frequencies, the exceptional-point condition, and the stability-threshold condition. We show that the largest absorption response is maximized by approaching the stability threshold from the stable side. Near the threshold on the stable side, the absorption spectrum exhibits strong enhancement and linewidth narrowing, together with pronounced helicity dependence in the sub-THz regime that can be switched by reversing the spin-orbit torque. We also confirm by solving the full LLG dynamics that crossing the threshold leads to gain and self-oscillation. These results identify the stability threshold as the key control principle for enhancing absorption and achieving polarization selectivity in the sub-THz/THz regime.
summary: The authors analyze antiferromagnetic resonance in an AFI/NM junction by treating the dynamics as a non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem. They demonstrate that maximizing absorption and achieving helicity selectivity requires tuning parameters near the stability threshold, which is distinct from the exceptional point. This establishes the stability boundary as the key control mechanism for developing polarization-selective sub-THz devices.
main_problem: The study investigates non-Hermitian control mechanisms governing helicity-selective antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) in magnetic junctions.
main_result: Strong resonant absorption enhancement and polarization selectivity are maximized by tuning the system parameters towards the stability threshold, rather than necessarily at the exceptional point. Reversing the spin-orbit torque can switch this helicity dependence.
method: The dynamics are analyzed by linearizing the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation into a 2x2 non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem to derive complex resonance frequencies and stability criteria.
model_or_system: The system is an antiferromagnetic insulator/nonmagnetic metal junction, modeled using sublattice-dependent damping and spin-orbit torque acting on one sublattice. The dynamics are governed by the linearized LLG equation.
key_observables: Complex resonance frequencies ($\omega_{\pm}$), stability threshold ($\Gamma_{max}=0$), absorption power ($P(\omega)$), and degree of circular polarization ($C(\omega)$).
important_parameters: Spin-orbit torque strength ($c_J$), damping parameters, and the proximity to the stability threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \ll 1$ and $H_J \gg H_0, H_D, c_J$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the junction setup, stability diagrams showing the boundary ($\Gamma_{max}=0$) relative to the Exceptional Point (EP), and resonance spectra demonstrating enhancement near the threshold.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by formulating the problem as a non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem, deriving conditions for EP and stability thresholds, analyzing absorption enhancement near these points, and finally confirming the results via full LLG dynamics to show gain/oscillation upon crossing the threshold.
why_interesting: This work applies concepts from non-Hermitian physics (EPs, stability boundaries) to classical magnetism, providing a framework for engineering highly controllable, polarization-selective THz devices using magnetic materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the antiferromagnetic insu- lator (AFI)/nonmagnetic metal (NM) junction considered in this study. The antiferromagnet consists of two sublattices, A and B, and is assumed to couple to the NM only through sublattice A. A charge current J flowing in the NM along the x direction induces a damping-like spin-orbit torque TA acting on the interfacial sublattice A. A static magnetic field H0 is applied along the z direction. The antiferromagnetic resonance driven by a circularly polarized THz wave is stud- ied.

FIG. 2. Stability diagram in the (α1, cJ) plane for H0 = 0 and α2 = 0.002. The color map shows Γmax = max [Im ω+, Im ω−]. The black line indicates the threshold condition Γmax = 0. The dashed and dotted lines represent Re D = 0 and Im D = 0, and their intersection (red dot) in- dicates the exceptional point (EP).

FIG. 3. Real and imaginary parts of the two resonance frequencies as a function of α1 for (a,b) cJ = 6.4×10−4 T and (c,d) cJ = 0.04 T. The point where the eigenvalues coalesce in (a) and (b) corresponds to the exceptional point (EP). The remaining parameters are set to H0 = 0 and α2 = 0.002.

Figure 4(a) shows the absorption spectra for cJ = 0.04 T as α1 approaches the stability threshold from the stable side (α1 > 0.0032). Far from the stability thresh- old, the absorption peaks have broad linewidths and rel- atively small peak intensities. In contrast, as the system approaches the stability boundary from the stable side, one peak becomes narrower and stronger, reflecting the approach of Im ω+ to zero.
